13

  • N: zizānam | i[nēru | nāʾe]ram | mupparšam | mubatt[iram]
  • T: The Cricket they [killed], the Screecher, the Flyer, the Worm,
  • L: zizānam ← zizānu I “(a cricket)? jB”; i[nēru ← nêru I “to strike”; nāʾe]ram ← nā'eru I “roaring O/jB of lion (figure), deity”; mupparšam ← mupparšu I “flying, winged OB, jB”; mubatt[iram] ← mubattiru I “(a worm or grub)? jB”
  • Note: See [RN117: 270]: “The word zi-za-na-am is curiously written, half on the tablet’s left edge. There are two possible meanings, (a) a kind of grasshopper or locust, well attested, and (b) a half-share or measure known only from the lexical entry MSL XVI, p. 162, Nabnītu XVII 238: ½.tar = zi-za-nu. Which is appropriate here — if either — is uncertain.” The new parallel in SB V 308 suggests the reading adopted [EJ].
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "V" 19; cf. L I.4 SB "V" 308

21-22a

  • N: mīnû | ubaššakka || qištam | ša <erēni> | šunēl
  • T: what can bring you dishonour? The forest of <cedar> wood (22) lay low!
  • L: mīnû ← mīnu I “what? OAkk, OB, MA, Nuzi, NB in PN”; ubaššakka ← bâšu I “to be ashamed, come to shame”; qištam ← qištu I “pl. qišātu(m) forest, wood q. erēnim cedar forest”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; <erēni> ← erēnu I “cedar OAkk qišti e. cedar forest”; šunēl ← nâlu I “to lie down (to sleep)”
  • Note: See [RN117: 271]: “GIŠ is probably defective for {giš}erēnim. More is missing if the line is to make sense as it stands, so I presume that šunēl belongs at the end and has slipped to l. 22 by mistake.”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "V" 304
BabaOB1 o 21-22a. mi-nu-u₂-um u₂-ba-ša-ka qi₂-iš-tam ša {giš}<EREN> | šu-ne₂-el

22b

  • N: šuwwiam | erēnam | šīham
  • T: Seek out for me a tall cedar,
  • L: šuwwiam ← še'û I “also šê'u to seek (out)”; erēnam ← erēnu I “cedar OAkk qišti e. cedar forest”; šīham ← šīhu I “grown (tall) Bab., NA of gods, men, physique”
  • Note: See [RN117: 271]: “Von Soden (‘die dir nun gehört’) and Hecker (‘deine’) took the second word as the accusative independent possessive pronoun, evidently reading ku-wa-a-am. However, the expected form in OB is kâm. Bottéro (‘un Cèdre extraordinairement élevé’) evidently parsed it as the accusative adjective šūpâm (cf. Tournay and Shaffer: šu-pi-a-am), but the uncontracted form would be šūpuʾam not šūpiʾam. I suppose it to be the verb šeʾûm in the imperative of the rare II/1 stem, with a glide in place of the glottal stop. This couplet exhibits an emphatic alliteration on /š/ lacking in the later version, which has ibrī nittakis erēna šīha / ša muhhašu šamê nakpu (SB V 293–4).”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "V" 314
BabaOB1 o 22b. šu-wi-a-am {giš}ERIN ši-ha-am

22c

  • N: ša muhhašu | šamāʾī | šannu
  • T: whose top vies with the heavens!
  • L: ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; muhhašu ← muhhu I “skull”; šamāʾī ← šamû I “mostly pl. tant. sky, heaven”; šannu ← šanānu I “to equal, rival”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "V" 315
BabaOB1 o 22c-23. ša mu-ha-šu | ($___$) ša-ma-A.A ša-an-nu

27

  • N: ana bīti (|) ellil | libil (|) pur[a]ttum
  • T: To the house of Enlil the Euphrates shall take it,
  • L: ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; bīti ← bītu I “m.”; ellil ← Ellil I “”; libil ← wabālu I “(cf. also babālu) to carry, bring”; pur[a]ttum ← Purattu I
  • Note: See [RN117: 271]: “As read the genitive construct state bīti either (a) retains its case-vowel, exhibiting the old-fashioned ending (as in OB II 165), or (b) exhibits crasis, bīt-Illil. One might instead read qá-ti, ‘to the hands of Enlil’.”
